The strokes

The tonbak's voice comes from a goat-skin head over a hollow mulberry body that narrows to an open bell. Where you strike it decides which system rings: the centre drives the air cavity and gives the deep Tom, the rim barely couples to it at all and gives the dry Bak. Every stroke below is modelled on that behaviour rather than sampled, so it responds to velocity and never repeats itself exactly.

Tap any stroke to hear it.

No stroke matches that.

Tune the drum

No two tonbaks sound alike — head tension, shell size and how dry the skin is on the day all move the tone. Adjust each stroke until it matches the drum you have in your ear. Changes are applied live, and are kept between sessions.

Start the loop below and tune while it plays, so you hear each stroke in context rather than on its own.

Send this back and it becomes the built-in tuning. Only the values you changed are listed.

Build a pattern

Set the metre, then tap the grid to place strokes. Tap a placed stroke again to cycle it from accented to normal to ghost.

Settings

Tonbak — Persian rhythm trainer.

Every stroke is synthesised from a physical model of the drum: coupled membrane modes and cavity resonance, rendered fresh at launch. Nothing is sampled and nothing is downloaded, so the app works with no network at all.
